title: King Oliver's practice habits; Lester never practised
summary: Oliver practised exercises and liked diminished chords, with a bigger tone than Louis; Lester never practised, only played.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Was King Oliver into practicing at the time you were with him?
Yeah, he practiced himself. He was in the room blowing his horn.
What kind of stuff did he practice?
He'd just be blowing over exercises and things. He was crazy about diminished chords.
Yeah. He'd sing... [SINGS] (and go back to the tonic) ..[SINGS] He used to play little cadenzas on his tunes. He'd run a diminished chord and then come back to the tonic.
So he would consciously insert it in there.

Yeah, he always liked them. They're pretty, too, those diminished chords. He had a tone that big. His tone was bigger than Louis. He had a big tone. I guess Louis was faster than he was, and Louis had a more modern feeling on his horn.
Anything else that he used to practice besides diminished patterns?
No. He'd just be running over his horn, just playing the exercises, like chromatic scales. Just exercises.
You mentioned before that Lester wasn't into practicing. Was he practicing at this time?
No. He never practiced. He'd take his horn and play. He warmed up.
Did he ever have any special warm-up exercises? Would you hear him play the same little phrases over and over to warm up with?
No. He'd pick it up and just played whatever I guess was in his mind. He didn't do it that long. I never heard him around blowing a horn and practicing. I never heard him practice. He'd just blow.
Anything else King taught you? Besides the shortcuts for not fingering all those notes up on the top?
No, that's about all he taught me.
